probe: argv wire contract: argument fidelity and negative policy cases

beforeThisChange.wire: arguments: "-c '<code>'" (a pre-quoted string), split in the guest with split_whitespace()

cases.why: python received the literal argument 'print(123)' including the quotes - a string expression that evaluates and is discarded, so a caller asking to print a number got a successful run with nothing printed

cases.observed: exit 1, SyntaxError: unterminated string literal on the fragment 'print(1,
cases.why: the whitespace split tore the code in half at the space

afterThisChange.wire: protocolVersion: 2 with an explicit argv array; no string is ever re-split

cases.description: embedded double quotes, single quotes, newlines, a tab and non-ASCII in one argument

negativeCases.description: a version 1 request (no protocolVersion, arguments as a string)
negativeCases.response: SPLAT refused the request: protocol version 1 is not supported. This daemon speaks version 2, which requires an explicit argv array.

negativeCases.description: a command that is not in its own lease's allowedExecPaths
negativeCases.response: SPLAT refused to execute: '/usr/bin/python3' is not in this lease's allowedExecPaths.

notProvenHere: The run was against --mock-bpf, so the kernel hooks were not loaded and allowedExecPaths was checked by the daemon rather than enforced by bprm_check_security. The coherence refusal above is a userspace guard that keeps a caller from getting a bare -EPERM; the enforcement behind it still needs the root run.
Bash and Node were not exercised, only Python. The argv path is language-agnostic by construction - nothing inspects the argument - but the audit asks for all three.
